newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-DORTMUND COACH STANDS FIRM OVER MOELLER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DORTMUND COACH STANDS FIRM OVER MOELLER.

text.p: Borussia Dortmund coach Nevio Scala said on Monday he had no intention of bowing to criticism from Andreas Moeller after playing the German international midfielder as a striker.
Moeller had complained about the switch after Dortmund lost to Schalke 1-0 on Saturday.
"I am sticking with my philosophy and will keep working on that," Scala said after a training session where he was involved in animated discussions with Moeller.
"There is no possibility of discussing it at the moment," added Scala, who took over at the European Cup winning-club from Ottmar Hitzfeld at the end of last season.
Moeller voiced his disappointment in the wake of Dortmund's poor start to the season -- they have just four points from three games.

"Two months ago we were the best team in Europe," Moeller said after the latest defeat. "Now Karlheinz Riedle is gone (to Liverpool), Stephane Chapusiat is out of the picture and I have been made a striker. You can just throw everything away."
But he was calmer on Monday, saying: "I had to let go of some frustration. Perhaps it was a mistake to say so much."
